catalog.title: Rational Hodge classes on mixed products of K3 moduli spaces

metadata.title: Rational Hodge classes on mixed products of K3 moduli spaces
metadata.description: Combining OpenAI's rational Hodge theorem for arbitrary mixed products of projective K3 surfaces with Bülles' Chow-motive decomposition, this note records rational Hodge in every codimension for finite mixed products of the smooth projective K3 moduli spaces covered by that decomposition. Bases may differ or repeat. The factors include Hilbert schemes, stable twisted-sheaf moduli, and eligible moduli of Bridgeland-stable objects, subject to the exact smoothness, projectivity and stability hypotheses stated in the paper. The explicit pull-push proof checks codimensions and the non-fine, empty and zero-dimensional cases. The contribution is an assembled corollary of the cited results, with prior conditional transfers by Arapura; it supplies no new proof of the base K3 theorem, no new motivic reduction, and no first or substantial independent novelty claim. The base input is the public OpenAI Math Release snapshot adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a, accessed October 6, 2026: https://github.com/openai/math/tree/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. Manuscript cover dates do not establish earliest public priority. No assertion is made about arbitrary K3^[n] deformations, singular or semistable moduli, abelian-surface moduli, integral or generalized Hodge, or finite-dimensional motives. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing; automated adversarial reviews are not human peer review. The supplementary exact finite checks certify only the stated algebraic computations; neither they nor the upstream Clifford Lean module formalize the full Hodge theorem.
references: T.-H. Bülles, Motives of moduli spaces on K3 surfaces and of special cubic fourfolds, Manuscripta Math. 161 (2020), 109–124. DOI: 10.1007/s00229-018-1086-0; arXiv:1806.08284v1, Theorem 0.1.

catalog.title: L2-acyclicity and cost for a rank-100 amalgam

metadata.title: L2-acyclicity and cost for a rank-100 amalgam
metadata.description:
An expanded consequence and verification note for OpenAI's rank-100 fixed-price construction. A self-contained regular-tree and cellular-boundary calculation proves that its displayed 101-generator/100-relator presentation complex is a finite two-dimensional classifying space and every L2-Betti number vanishes, independently of either cost bound. Gaboriau's action invariance and OpenAI's positive Bernoulli cost estimate then give an explicit free ergodic p.m.p. orbit relation with Cost at least 1 + 1/(100*2^61) and vanishing L2-Betti numbers. The group infimum cost is one.

The group and positive cost estimate are due to OpenAI; cost--Betti comparison and action invariance are due to Gaboriau. The general fixed-price implication was already explicit in Popa--Shlyakhtenko--Vaes, and the short conditional limit argument was already in the author's public preliminary triage. Added content is the direct all-degree invariant proof and reproducible input-validation record. No independent fixed-price discovery or firstness is claimed. The pinned upstream source warns that its source argument was intermediate. Its pivotal proof is explicitly identified and independently audited in the supplement.

AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and adversarial verification. At publication this preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing. Automated audits are neither human refereeing nor machine formalization. catalog.title: Signed impulse estimates and global smooth solutions for finite multispecies relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell

metadata.title: Signed impulse estimates and global smooth solutions for finite multispecies relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell
metadata.description: This research note extends the signed-impulse argument of OpenAI family 362 to a fixed finite number of relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell species with positive masses and arbitrary real charges. It derives the exact source-receiver coefficient, positive mass-weighted energy, angular occupation and selected coefficient bounds, and one coupled momentum bootstrap. The stated global classical theorem assumes nonnegative smooth compact phase data and compatible Maxwell fields with bounded derivatives of all orders and finite energy. The one-species result and its analytic machinery are attributed to OpenAI; mass normalization and continuation are established kinetic theory. No firstness or full Lean-formalization claim is made. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. The preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing; automated adversarial audits are not human peer review. The universal geometric cancellation is inherited; the new contribution is its species-dependent coefficient transfer and coupled closure for distinct charge-to-mass ratios. Constants may depend on the fixed finite species list; no massless limit or noncompact momentum-tail extension is asserted.

metadata.description:

catalog.title: Two consequences of group-algebra and planar Fourier certificates: wreath products and triangle bounds

metadata.title: Two consequences of group-algebra and planar Fourier certificates: wreath products and triangle bounds
metadata.description: We derive two separately motivated consequences of precisely identified input theorems in OpenAI's mathematics collection. The torsion-free group-algebra counterexample, combined with the established Hopfian embedding framework, yields a finitely generated Hopfian group H for which the standard restricted regular wreath product C2 wr H is non-Hopfian. We give its split epimorphism and kernel explicitly. The sharp planar two-point Fourier certificate, combined with the Cohn-de Laat-Salmon product-program comparison and triangular-lattice Poisson bounds, yields L2=2/sqrt(3) and the exact planar triangle infimum P2=4/3. We reconstruct the deductions, audit the substantive inputs, repair product-proof bookkeeping, and provide independently implemented validated computations and source records. These consequences use credited literature; no first-priority or independent-breakthrough claim is made. The planar equality does not settle the all-dimensional triangle problem or assert attainment of its infimum. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting, computation and verification. Internal independent and adversarial reviews were AI-assisted. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing. AI systems are not authors; no external endorsement is implied. The associated Lean artifacts concern another construction and do not formally verify these results.

metadata.title: Pure-loss bosonic dynamic capacities: EPnI consequences and consumed-key secrecy accounting
metadata.description: The finite-energy multimode entropy photon-number inequality in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies the sharp entropy premise for the previously conditional pure-loss bosonic classical/quantum/entanglement capacity region under an average photon constraint, including arbitrary entanglement across channel uses. This note gives the precise consequence and audits a private-resource operational defect: the printed catalytic secrecy condition in the cited coding theorem protects consumed key jointly with generated secrets and excludes the one-time pad. catalog.title: Even Minkowski uniqueness as a consequence of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski

metadata.title: Even Minkowski uniqueness as a consequence of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski
metadata.description: This research note records consequences of OpenAI's recently released origin-symmetric logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality. In every ambient dimension n >= 2 and for 0 <= p < 1, every smooth strictly positive even density on S^(n-1) has exactly one smooth positive even support-function solution of h^(1-p) det(∇²h+hI)=f with positive-definite curvature-radius matrix. For 0 < p < 1, identical Lp surface-area measures determine arbitrary full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies. The note gives the nonsmooth first-variation and mixed-volume strictness argument explicitly and a local form of the smooth endpoint transfer of He–Liu; existence and regularity are established inputs. These results are newly available consequences of the new inequality and known reductions, not a new proof of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski or a claim of first public announcement. Equal-volume boxes exclude arbitrary-measure uniqueness at p=0. The package contains source, analytic and priority audits, pinned dependency hashes and reproducible exact rational checks. The upstream Lean source scope was inspected, but independent kernel rebuilding, axiom extraction and Comparator reproduction were not completed; no formal verification of this follow-on theorem is claimed. catalog.title: Hypersingular Riesz-energy constants on surfaces from triangular-lattice universal optimality

metadata.title: Hypersingular Riesz-energy constants on surfaces from triangular-lattice universal optimality
metadata.description:
This consequence note records the exact ordered-pair two-dimensional hypersingular Riesz-energy constant for every real s > 2: C_(s,2) = zeta_Lambda(s), with Lambda the covolume-one triangular lattice. For every smooth compact embedded surface with positive area A, including smooth boundary and using ambient Euclidean distance, the minimal ordered energy is asymptotic to zeta_Lambda(s) A^(-s/2) N^(1+s/2). The unit sphere coefficient is zeta_Lambda(s)/(4 pi)^(s/2).

OpenAI's recently released planar universal-energy theorem is the substantive new input. The finite/periodic reduction and manifold universality are established results of Hardin, Saff, Simanek, Leble and Serfaty, with periodic averaging credited to Cohn and Kumar. We give a self-contained gap-periodization account with exact pair, density, covolume and tail conventions. The target is the dimension-two s > 2 case of Brauchart-Hardin-Saff Conjecture 2, originally posed for the sphere by Kuijlaars and Saff. No independent base breakthrough or first-public-priority claim is made.

The upstream analytic arguments were independently audited and their finite certificates reproduced. Actual Lean source semantics were inspected, but a complete pinned Lean/Mathlib build was not reproduced; no formal-verification claim is made. catalog.title: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds

metadata.title: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds
metadata.description: Explicit fixed-binary-alphabet consequences of OpenAI's two relation-liveness lower bounds. A strict h-squared adjacency-block language has a one-way nondeterministic source with (3h^3-h)/2+2 endmarked states, and an ordinary epsilon-free source with one fewer state. Equivalent two-way deterministic automata and two-way nondeterministic automata for its full binary complement require 2^Omega(h), hence 2^Omega(n^(1/3)) in the cubic source size. The note gives exact transitions, an sh^2-state pullback, all-word complement semantics, and an h^3 fooling-set source lower bound. The exponential obstructions are inherited from OpenAI; binary coding is established machinery, attributed to earlier work. AI tools were used extensively. catalog.title: A fixed moment separator without a rational normalized sum-of-squares certificate

metadata.title: A fixed moment separator without a rational normalized sum-of-squares certificate
metadata.description:
This research note exhibits the phenomenon asked about in the literal fixed-polynomial certificate question in Oberwolfach Report 14/2023, under an explicit rational polynomial-square convention. On the rational unit ball in three variables, p=1+f for Scheiderer's classical quartic has minimum one and annihilates an explicit rational degree-four moment vector of mass one. It belongs to 1+Q_R(g) but not to 1+Q_Q(g), even with arbitrary finite multiplier degrees. The input moment matrix is not positive semidefinite. A different polynomial q=1+x^4 certifies the same vector rationally, p itself is rationally positivity-certifiable, and every rational rescaling cp with c>1 has a rational normalized certificate. The result is outside the companion preprint's strict-margin regime and asserts no algorithm, minimal degree or general descent theorem.

The contribution is an explicit normalized-moment application and scope clarification of established ingredients. Scheiderer's quartic and field obstruction, the classical leading-form/completion mechanism, Benoist's formal-ring observation, Nie's earlier ball application, the prior irrational Gram and Naldi-Sinn semidefinite-infeasibility applications, and Powers' strictly positive rational certificate are credited. The portable archive supplies the manuscript source, all 35 exact rational moments and sparse polynomial data, a Python-standard-library checker with its complete byte-identical expected 2,059-check output, claim and priority notes, publication metadata, source-version provenance and a file-hash manifest. Finite computations supplement the written Galois and all-degree local proofs; they are not finite-search proofs of arbitrary-degree impossibility.

Three independently initiated bounded priority families identified no exact earlier normalized-moment application in the primary passages inspected. catalog.title: Nonconvexity of fixed odd-power sum-of-squares cones

metadata.title: Nonconvexity of fixed odd-power sum-of-squares cones
metadata.description:
This research note gives a negative answer to the general-dimensional fixed odd-power convexity question recorded by Reznick in Oberwolfach Reports 14/2023 and repeated by Blekherman, Kozhasov and Reznick in 2026. For real nonnegative homogeneous sextics whose cubes are sums of squares, the cone is nonconvex in the explicit finite dimension 3*10^62: disjoint copies of the classical coefficient-1 modified Motzkin seed have SOS cubes, while their finite average does not. For every fixed odd exponent q>=3, some finite dimension n(q) gives nonconvexity. No ternary result, minimal dimension, uniform dimension for all exponents or full classification is claimed. Closedness and the earlier convexity of the union over odd exponents remain consistent.

The proof applies classical SOS separation, product truncated-functional positivity and elementary distinct-index counting. The exact seed, its SOS cube and the standard separation, tensor and collision ingredients are credited to earlier primary sources. An explicit rational order-nine moment functional yields the displayed dimension. The verification archive supplies the standalone manuscript source, all 20 initial minors and 24 exact Schur traces, a Python-standard-library checker with full 220 local LDL positivity/reconstruction, exact cube/moment/sign checks, complete expected output, hash/provenance records, claim scope and a dated priority note. The arbitrary finite tensor argument and the general odd-exponent result are proved analytically, not by constructing an astronomical matrix.

Two independent extensive bounded priority audits identified no exact earlier fixed-power result in the sources inspected. catalog.title: A telescoping proof of the focal antipedal sum invariant

metadata.title: A telescoping proof of the focal antipedal sum invariant
metadata.description:
This preprint proves the focal antipedal distance-sum equality observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller as elliptic billiard invariant k603. For every regular closed billiard/Poncelet orbit between strictly nested confocal ellipses, lambda strictly between zero and b squared, the ordinary positive radial-distance sums of the two focal antipedal polygons agree. The proof identifies their per-edge norm difference with a fixed coefficient times the vertical displacement, then uses closure. It covers odd primitive periods, admitted stars, reversal and repeated traversal, without asserting separate constancy of either sum or extending to hyperbolic or degenerate caustics. Standard-library exact rational-chord verification accompanies the self-contained proof.

catalog.title: NP-completeness of aggregate root-dependent spanning-tree cost

metadata.title: NP-completeness of aggregate root-dependent spanning-tree cost
metadata.description:
For one common undirected spanning tree, every vertex root induces a whole-tree orientation whose arc costs are independently supplied. This preprint proves NP-completeness of deciding whether the sum of all root costs is at most a threshold, even with costs in {0,1,2}; a uniform shift gives costs in {1,2,3}. The self-contained satisfiability reduction resolves Problem 1 in Volker Kaibel's November 2018 Oberwolfach workshop contribution, whose report was published in December 2019. Standard-library exact verification files accompany the proof.

No earlier proof of the exact objective was located in the bounded source and model audit completed on 6 October 2026; no absolute-first or continued-open-status claim is made.
